name: Sicilian Defense
summary: The most combative, asymmetric, and popular response to 1.e4. Black fights for central control from the flank and creates winning chances without settling for symmetry.
keyConcepts: d4 pawn break vs d6/e6 pawn structures

subVariations.name: Sicilian Najdorf: English Attack / Main Lines
subVariations.description: The Rolls-Royce of chess openings. With 5...a6 Black controls b5 and prepares queenside expansion with ...b5.
subVariations.whitePlan: Castle queenside (O-O-O), launch pawn storm with f3, g4, h4, and breakthrough on d5.
subVariations.blackPlan: Expand on queenside with ...b5, exert pressure on c-file, counterstrike with ...d5.

subVariations.name: Sicilian Najdorf: Adams Attack (6.h3)
subVariations.description: White plays 6.h3 aiming for g4 and Bg2 without committing the center early, popularized by Weaver Adams and Bobby Fischer.
subVariations.whitePlan: Play g4, Bg2, Nde2-g3, exerting positional kingside control.
subVariations.blackPlan: Clamp White's g4 with 7...h5, develop ...Be7 and ...Nbd7, counter on queenside.

subVariations.name: Sicilian Najdorf: Poisoned Pawn Variation (6.Bg5 e6 7.f4 Qb6)
subVariations.description: The legendary Poisoned Pawn variation favored by Bobby Fischer and Garry Kasparov. Black grabs the b2 pawn with the queen, surviving incredible tactical pressure.
subVariations.whitePlan: Trap or harangue Black's queen, sacrifice pieces for a decisive mating attack.
subVariations.blackPlan: Hold onto material, navigate tactical minefields, consolidate for a winning endgame.

subVariations.name: Sicilian Najdorf: Classical 6.Be2 Variation
subVariations.description: Anatoly Karpov's positional masterpiece setup. White avoids wild pawn storms in favor of central prophylaxis and control of d5.
subVariations.whitePlan: Control d5 outpost, clamp queenside with a4-a5, maneuver Nd5.
subVariations.blackPlan: Play ...Qc7, ...Rfd8, prepare ...d5 central breakthrough.

subVariations.name: Sicilian Dragon: Yugoslav Attack (9.Bc4)
subVariations.description: The ferocious Yugoslav Attack with 9.Bc4. A mutual mating race where White storms the h-file while Black attacks down the c-file.
subVariations.whitePlan: Trade dark bishops via Bh6, blast open the h-file with h4-h5, sacrifice to checkmate.
subVariations.blackPlan: Counter down c-file with ...Nc4, sacrifice exchange on c3 (...Rxc3), crush White's king.

subVariations.name: Sicilian Dragon: Yugoslav 9.O-O-O (Soltis Variation)
subVariations.description: Black counters immediately in the center with 12...d5!, forcing sharp central piece play rather than pure flank attacks.
subVariations.whitePlan: Target c6 and exchange dark bishops with Bd4.
subVariations.blackPlan: Sacrifice the exchange on f8 for immense bishop pair activity on e6/g7.

subVariations.name: Sicilian Dragon: Classical 6.Be2 System
subVariations.description: White castles short and plays f4, allowing a positional and classical middlegame.
subVariations.whitePlan: Push f5 to dislodge Black's light-squared bishop and attack the kingside.
subVariations.blackPlan: Place knight on c4 via Na5, pressure queenside pawns and e-file.

subVariations.name: Sicilian Scheveningen: Classical Setup
subVariations.description: The classical 'small center' pawn formation with d6 and e6, a bedrock of World Championship strategy.
subVariations.whitePlan: Aim for kingside pressure via f4-f5 or g4, or pressure d6.
subVariations.blackPlan: Maintain flexible center, coordinate pieces on c/e files, break with ...e5 or ...d5.

subVariations.name: Sicilian Scheveningen: Keres Attack (6.g4)
subVariations.description: Paul Keres's feared 6.g4 thrust, instantly contesting the kingside and dislodging Black's f6-knight.
subVariations.whitePlan: Push g5, open the g-file with Rg1, crush Black's kingside.
subVariations.blackPlan: Strike back in the center with 8...d5, opening lines for active pieces.

subVariations.name: Sicilian Sveshnikov: Chelyabinsk Main Line
subVariations.description: Black willingly accepts a backward d6-pawn and a hole on d5 in exchange for huge active piece play and bishop pair.
subVariations.whitePlan: Anchor d5 knight, target d6 backward pawn, restrict Black's ...f5 break.
subVariations.blackPlan: Use dark-squared bishop pair, push ...f5 to create kingside counterplay.

subVariations.name: Sicilian Kalashnikov: 4...e5 System
subVariations.description: Black plays 4...e5 without 4...Nf6, trading off the dark-squared bishops with ...Bg5 to solve positional problems.
subVariations.whitePlan: Establish Maróczy Bind clamp with c4 and control d5.
subVariations.blackPlan: Trade dark bishops via ...Bg5, maneuver knights to f6 and c5, pressure e4.

subVariations.name: Sicilian Classical: Richter-Rauzer Attack
subVariations.description: White pins the knight with 6.Bg5 and damages Black's pawn structure with Bxf6, leading to sharp struggles.
subVariations.whitePlan: Castle long, push e5 or f5, attack down the d-file and kingside.
subVariations.blackPlan: Utilize open g-file and bishop pair, counterattack on queenside with ...b4.

subVariations.name: Sicilian Classical: Sozin / Velimirovic Attack
subVariations.description: Bobby Fischer's favorite weapon against the Classical. White targets e6 and f7 with Bc4 and launches a venomous attack with Qe2 and g4.
subVariations.whitePlan: Push g4-g5, sacrifice on e6 or d5, mate the black king.
subVariations.blackPlan: Coordinate pieces via ...Nd7-c5, trade the dangerous b3 bishop, attack c-file.

subVariations.name: Sicilian Taimanov: Bastrikov System
subVariations.description: Smooth piece coordination without committing the d-pawn early. Black strikes with an active ...Bb4 and central ...d5.
subVariations.whitePlan: Employ English Attack setup (Be3/Qd2/f3/g4) or clamp with c4.
subVariations.blackPlan: Pin with ...Bb4, break with ...d5, dominate central light squares.

subVariations.name: Sicilian Kan: Paulsen System
subVariations.description: Ultra-flexible hedgehog-style system with 2...e6 and 4...a6, keeping maximum options open.
subVariations.whitePlan: Establish Maróczy Bind with c4/d4 to suppress Black's breaks.
subVariations.blackPlan: Build Hedgehog fortress with ...b6, ...Bb7, ...d6, break with ...b5 or ...d5.

subVariations.name: Sicilian Accelerated Dragon: Maróczy Bind
subVariations.description: Black plays 4...g6 immediately, avoiding 2...d6 to threaten an immediate ...d7-d5 break.
subVariations.whitePlan: Clamp down on d5 with c4/e4 pawns, restrict Black's breaks.
subVariations.blackPlan: Trade minor pieces, pressure e4 with ...Bc6, prepare ...f5 or ...b5 counterplay.

subVariations.name: Sicilian Hyper-Accelerated Dragon (2...g6)
subVariations.description: Black fianchettoes on move 2! Sharp Queen sorties arise after 4.Qxd4 Nf6 5.e5 Nc6.
subVariations.whitePlan: Harass Black's knights with e5 and Qe4, maintain central control.
subVariations.blackPlan: Anchor knights safely on b4/c6, develop the monster g7 bishop, counterattack.

subVariations.name: Sicilian Alapin: 2.c3 with 2...d5
subVariations.description: White plays 2.c3 to establish a solid d4 pawn center, leading to thematic Isolated Queen Pawn (IQP) battles.
subVariations.whitePlan: Use active pieces around the d4 IQP, attack down the e-file and kingside.
subVariations.blackPlan: Blockade d5 square, trade minor pieces to enter a superior endgame against the IQP.

subVariations.name: Sicilian Alapin: 2.c3 with 2...Nf6
subVariations.description: Black counter-attacks e4 immediately with 2...Nf6, leading to fluid piece play and central friction.
subVariations.whitePlan: Maintain e5 space wedge, develop active bishop on c4, create kingside threats.
subVariations.blackPlan: Undermine e5 with ...d6, fianchetto queenside bishop on b7, pressure d4.

subVariations.name: Closed Sicilian: Spassky System
subVariations.description: Boris Spassky's World Championship weapon. White avoids 3.d4 and builds a positional kingside attack with g3/f4.
subVariations.whitePlan: Advance f4-f5 or g4-g5 to mate on the kingside, utilizing the g2 bishop.
subVariations.blackPlan: Occupy d4 outpost with ...Nd4, expand on queenside with ...Rb8 and ...b5.

subVariations.name: Grand Prix Attack (2.Nc3 & 3.f4)
subVariations.description: An aggressive attacking setup for White with an early f4 and Bc4, aiming to puncture Black's kingside defenses.
subVariations.whitePlan: Sacrifice f5 to disrupt Black's structure, attack with Qe1-h4 and Bh6.
subVariations.blackPlan: Blunt Bc4 with ...d5, expand on queenside with ...b5, exploit light squares.

subVariations.name: Sicilian Rossolimo: 3.Bb5 vs 2...Nc6
subVariations.description: A favorite of Magnus Carlsen. White trades the bishop for the knight on c6, inflicting doubled c-pawns on Black.
subVariations.whitePlan: Castle long, control d5, exploit doubled pawns and clamp Black's counterplay.
subVariations.blackPlan: Utilize bishop pair, control center with ...e5, organize queenside counterplay.

subVariations.name: Sicilian Moscow: 3.Bb5+ vs 2...d6
subVariations.description: White delivers a check on b5 to force bishop exchanges, simplifying into a controlled positional middlegame.
subVariations.whitePlan: Build pawn center with c3/d4, push e5, establish kingside spatial advantage.
subVariations.blackPlan: Anchor knight on e4, challenge e5 pawn, counterattack along c-file.

subVariations.name: Smith-Morra Gambit Accepted
subVariations.description: White sacrifices a pawn on move 3 for blazing development and open c- and d-files aimed at Black's king.
subVariations.whitePlan: Pressure d6 with Rd1 and Bc4, sacrifice pieces on d5/e6 to breach the king.
subVariations.blackPlan: Solidify with ...e6 and ...e5, return pawn if needed to secure superior endgame.
